claims.text: Retention of toughness in demanding HEAs is governed by the stability and coherence of fine-scale precipitates.
Controlled thermal aging at intermediate temperatures will cause precipitate coarsening and may induce phase transformation.
Fine, coherent, well-distributed precipitates allow toughness to be retained or improved relative to the baseline.
Precipitates that become too large or lose coherence cause toughness to decrease.
An as-cast or rapidly quenched equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn or related HEA can have a homogeneous single- or dual-phase microstructure containing fine coherent precipitates.
Aging between 550 °C and 700 °C is an appropriate range for precipitate evolution without complete phase decomposition.
An inert atmosphere during aging will preclude oxidation.
Fine coherent precipitates mediate dislocation motion by being sheared by or pinning dislocations.
Fine coherent precipitates act as barriers against crack initiation.
Coherent precipitate structures favor planar dislocation slip across coherent interfaces.
Shearing of coherent precipitate structures can accommodate large local strain, alleviate stress concentration, and avoid crack formation.
Coarsening, coherency loss, or formation of brittle phases creates stress-concentration sites that facilitate crack initiation and propagation.
Aging that causes significant precipitate coarsening or coherency loss will produce a pronounced decrease in fracture toughness or impact energy.
The proposed mechanism applies to refractory and eutectic HEAs under moderate aging temperatures below 700 °C.
The mechanism applies where solid-solution strengthening and precipitate formation are balanced.
Critical precipitate-size and coherency thresholds vary with alloy system and processing history.
Grain size and residual stresses may modulate the relationship between precipitate state and toughness.
The hypothesis is falsified if coarsened or incoherent precipitates do not reduce toughness, or if fine coherent precipitates are retained while toughness decreases.
